name: Belgian below-threshold contract feed
demand: No verified search-volume, install, active-user, or paying-supplier count found. Statbel reports 1,202,139 Belgian VAT-registered enterprises at 31 Dec 2025; this is a broad ceiling, not the addressable market. BOSA reports 56,973 contracts registered on e-Procurement in 2024, of which 25,709 were published; these are procurement records, not evidence of willingness to pay. GPC Gov claims 500+ Belgian companies use its service, but its homepage also renders its client-company counter as 0, so treat that claim as unverified. Sources: https://statbel.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/vat-registered-businesses/vat-registered-enterprises ; https://bosa.belgium.be/nl/over-de-fod-bosa/jaarverslag-2024/overheidsopdrachten-2024 ; https://www.gpcgov.be/en
prices: GPC Gov currently lists Essential from €758/year excl. VAT or €80/month, and Professional from €1,299/year or €136/month; Essential advertises daily alerts and non-published below-threshold contracts. These are list prices, not verified sales. BOSA e-Procurement is free and offers supplier search profiles with daily email alerts in its enterprise manual. Aanbestedingsradar lists a free plan, Match at €270/month when billed annually (€3,240/year), and Bid Office at €450/month when billed annually. Aanbestedingen Radar lists free, €29/month, and €79/month plans. Polytender price: unverified. Sources: https://www.gpcgov.be/en/pricing ; https://bosa.belgium.be/sites/default/files/content/documents/manual_eproc_um_enterprises_en.pdf ; https://aanbestedingsradar.be/en/ ; https://aanbestedingenradar.be/ ; https://polytender.com/en/changelog
copy_speed: A direct copy of the published-notice layer appeared on 22 Oct 2026: Polytender says it added Belgium BOSA coverage for every notice, including notices below EU thresholds, plus awards and winner data. That does not establish coverage of genuinely unpublished direct invitations. Aanbestedingsradar is another live BOSA/TED matcher, but I found no verified launch date for it. No dated revenue event or independent proof of GPC Gov sales was found. Sources: https://polytender.com/en/changelog ; https://aanbestedingsradar.be/en/ ; https://www.gpcgov.be/en
platform_risk: Medium-high. BOSA provides free access to public procurement publications and runs a free platform; it also supports supplier search and direct invitations for unpublished contracts. Its terms require compliant use and prohibit disclosure of confidential content. Belgian public-sector information can be reusable commercially, but licenses, third-party rights, and access exceptions can apply. GPC Gov says its exclusive below-threshold records come directly from municipalities and public bodies, but I found no source-by-source provenance, reuse license, or access method. Verify those before building around the feed. Sources: https://bosa.belgium.be/en/conditions-use-and-availability-services-e-procurement-platform ; https://demo.publicprocurement.be/ ; https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/intellectual-property/innovation-and-intellectual/intellectual-property-public ; https://www.gpcgov.be/en
defensible_asset: Potential data moat only if the founder can lawfully maintain a demonstrably broader, fresher, source-linked dataset of actionable local opportunities. The official BOSA/TED notice layer is readily substitutable: BOSA is free and Polytender added direct BOSA coverage on 22 Oct 2026. GPC Gov claims exclusive municipal-source coverage, but the source list and record-level evidence are unverified. A feed alone has little network effect; switching costs could become moderate only if users accumulate valuable saved searches, matching history, and workflow records. Sources: https://www.gpcgov.be/en ; https://www.gpcgov.be/en/pricing ; https://polytender.com/en/changelog ; https://bosa.belgium.be/en/conditions-use-and-availability-services-e-procurement-platform
build_effort: Moderate for a self-serve BOSA/TED alert product; high for the differentiating local-source dataset. The product needs ingestion, deduplication, Dutch/French/German handling, matching, alerts, and source links. GPC Gov advertises human validation and dedicated client support, which suggests the incumbent workflow may contain ongoing service work. Biggest unknown is source access, provenance, and rights, not the matching interface. No reliable delivery-time estimate until a sample source audit is done. Sources: https://www.gpcgov.be/en/services ; https://be.linkedin.com/company/gpc-gov ; https://polytender.com/en/changelog
channel: Use inbound SEO pages by Belgian region, language, sector, and CPV category; software-directory and marketplace listings; product-led integrations; and paid search where compliant. Make tender alerts opt-in and avoid cold email, SMS, DMs, and calls. UK ICO guidance distinguishes individual subscribers, including sole traders, from corporate subscribers; the proposed inbound route avoids relying on unsolicited-message rules. Sources: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/advice-for-small-organisations/direct-marketing-and-data-protection/marketing-and-data-protection-in-detail/ ; https://www.gpcgov.be/en/pricing
owner_hours_per_week: Estimated target: 3–5 hours/week after steady state, unverified. This depends on permissioned, stable sources and no bespoke curation or consulting.
automation_reason: Estimate for a product-led feed: agents can ingest, deduplicate, classify, match, send opted-in alerts, handle billing and onboarding, and resolve routine support. Reserve human review for source permissions, feed failures, disputed records, and exceptional customer issues. This share is not measured; manual curation of private or fragmented local sources could push automation below 50%. GPC Gov says experts validate selections and advertises dedicated client contact, showing that its current service model is not proof of this automation target. Sources: https://be.linkedin.com/company/gpc-gov ; https://www.gpcgov.be/en/about
moat_assessment: Conditional data moat; not yet evidenced. BOSA identifies a €30,000 low-value threshold and a negotiated procedure without prior publication, while GPC Gov claims it captures such opportunities through exclusive municipal sources. Those records are the only plausible durable advantage; verify that they are actionable, source-linked, refreshable, and lawfully reusable. Published notices and basic saved searches are not defensible against free BOSA and fast-following aggregators. Sources: https://bosa.belgium.be/en/public-procurement-rules-and-procedures ; https://www.gpcgov.be/en ; https://polytender.com/en/changelog
desk_test: Zero-cost, manual, within one workday: take 20 GPC Gov records labelled unpublished from its no-sign-up trial; for each, capture the original source URL, date, deadline/status, buyer, and whether a supplier can access it without an invitation. Compare each against BOSA and Polytender. Record duplicates, missing source links, and any reuse terms. The test is to establish whether a distinct, actionable public-source dataset exists; do not automate collection until access and reuse conditions are checked. Sources: https://www.gpcgov.be/en ; https://demo.publicprocurement.be/ ; https://polytender.com/en/changelog ; https://bosa.belgium.be/en/conditions-use-and-availability-services-e-procurement-platform
red_flags: No verified revenue, payment event date, churn, customer count, or willingness-to-pay evidence. Current list prices do not prove sales. GPC Gov's homepage claim of 500+ companies conflicts with a client-company counter rendered as 0. Its core claim—non-published opportunities from exclusive municipal sources—has no public source-by-source proof in the pages reviewed. BOSA offers free search profiles, and Polytender added Belgian BOSA notices on 22 Oct 2026, so the published-notice feed is already being copied. Sources: https://www.gpcgov.be/en ; https://www.gpcgov.be/en/pricing ; https://bosa.belgium.be/sites/default/files/content/documents/manual_eproc_um_enterprises_en.pdf ; https://polytender.com/en/changelog
